summary:
iter-57 · Phase 1 security & reliability hardening verification. Backend: 176/176 unit tests pass (`pytest -m unit -q`, 5.8s). 225/225 http-sample tests pass (backend_test.py + iter80_password_reset + iter12_settings_2fa + iter22_security_hardening, 116s). New iter-57 phase-1 test file added (`tests/test_iter57_phase1_hardening.py`, 10/10 pass, 6.2s) covering health endpoints, admin-login cookie triple (access/refresh/csrf), CSRF enforce fail+pass (via raw urllib to bypass conftest CSRF injection), refresh rotation + family revocation on reuse, 6-fail login rate-limit lockout, logout server-side refresh revocation, password-change all-session revocation. Live WebSocket cookie-auth works (emits `connected` msg); ws?token= query auth is rejected (403) as expected. Frontend: production login flow works, all three cookies (access_token httpOnly, refresh_token httpOnly, csrf_token httpOnly=false) set on login, dashboard renders, no ErrorBoundary. Bot Config page renders all 8 presets in required order (Adaptive first, then Sniper/Scalper/Fast Scalp/Trend Rider/Breakout/Mean Reversion/Balanced). Scalp Fast Path + MT5 Accounts render. NO console CSRF 403 loop for GET-only navigation.

HOWEVER: **CRITICAL PRODUCTION BUG DISCOVERED**. Real-browser cookie-authenticated mutating requests are BLOCKED by the CSRF Origin allowlist check. Reproduced end-to-end by clicking Apply on the Adaptive preset in Bot Config UI → visible red UI banner: 'Request blocked by CSRF protection. Refresh and retry.' The backend rejects with 403 `{code:'csrf_failed', reason:'origin_not_allowed'}`. Also breaks silent-refresh interceptor (validated by nulling access_token cookie → refresh loop returns 403 origin_not_allowed → 403 → 403 → stays broken; user gets 'Invalid token' errors on subsequent API calls without recovery). Root cause: the Origin header seen by the backend arrives as `https://algo-trade-135.cluster-12.preview.emergentcf.cloud` (internal kube-cluster hostname injected by ingress) NOT the public `https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com` origin the browser actually issues (confirmed via temporary debug log — I added a one-line warn to /app/backend/security.py:143 which captured raw_env='https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com,http://localhost:3000' vs origin='https://algo-trade-135.cluster-12.preview.emergentcf.cloud'; log reverted before finishing). This did not surface in main-agent curl verification because plain curl does not send Origin — pytest suites (2163+ tests) all pass because they too don't set Origin, so the check is short-circuited by the `if allowed and origin` guard. In a real browser this blocks EVERY cookie-auth mutating call (login itself passes because at login time no auth cookies exist yet, so the has_cookie_auth branch is skipped).

critical.endpoint: middleware csrf_check in /app/backend/security.py (lines 139-143) — impacts ALL cookie-auth POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE including /api/auth/refresh, /api/bot/preset/*, /api/bot/config, /api/auth/change-password, /api/accounts/*, /api/settings/*
critical.issue: Origin allowlist rejects the internal cluster-injected Origin header. Browser sends Origin=https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com but backend receives origin='https://algo-trade-135.cluster-12.preview.emergentcf.cloud'. CORS_ORIGINS only allowlists the public preview domain, so every real-browser cookie-auth mutation returns 403 csrf_failed/origin_not_allowed. Silent-refresh interceptor also gets 403 loop, breaking auto token refresh.

ui_bugs.component: Bot Config → Apply preset (and any other mutating action)
ui_bugs.issue: Red banner 'Request blocked by CSRF protection. Refresh and retry.' after clicking apply on a preset. Same root cause as backend issue above — cannot POST /api/bot/preset/{key} from real browser.

Interceptor code is correct (attaches X-CSRF-Token from cookie, single-flight, retry-once, csrf_failed retry via /api/auth/csrf), but the backend rejects with origin_not_allowed so the retry can never succeed. When user's 30-min access_token expires, they get 'Invalid token' errors on every API call and must re-login manually.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix CSRF origin allowlist to accept the internal cluster-injected Origin. Two options: (a) Add the cluster origin (or a *.preview.emergentcf.cloud wildcard match) to CORS_ORIGINS handling in /app/backend/security.py:_allowed_origins / csrf_check, OR (b) change the strategy: skip the origin check when the request's Referer origin matches an allowed origin (browsers set Referer independently from Origin and it will point at the frontend URL the user actually loaded), OR (c) trust the request when Host header matches the cluster ingress and cookies+csrf-header double-submit already passed (double-submit already prevents CSRF, the Origin check is belt-and-suspenders). Recommended: add the *.emergentcf.cloud cluster suffix pattern to the allowlist, or check Origin against the request's own Host (same-site) as a fallback.

MINOR: Consider a `curl -H 'Origin: https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com' ...` regression test in the http suite so this class of bug is caught next time. Current conftest doesn't set Origin, so curl+pytest are blind to it.
critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL · Origin allowlist bug: /app/backend/security.py `_allowed_origins()` returns {https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com, http://localhost:3000} but Kubernetes ingress rewrites Origin to https://algo-trade-135.cluster-12.preview.emergentcf.cloud — a domain neither the user nor the frontend controls. Every browser-issued mutation gets 403. Belt-and-suspenders origin check is stricter than the double-submit CSRF token, and in this deployment topology it fails-closed for legitimate traffic. Reproduction: curl -H 'Origin: https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com' -H 'X-CSRF-Token: <cookie>' -b cookies.txt /api/auth/refresh returns 403. Fix by relaxing / augmenting _allowed_origins to include the cluster domain OR removing origin_not_allowed short-circuit when the CSRF double-submit check would pass. Double-submit already provides CSRF protection independently.

OK · CSRF double-submit token math (cookie value == X-CSRF-Token header, timing-safe compare) works correctly. csrf_token cookie is JS-readable (httpOnly=false), other auth cookies are httpOnly, SameSite=None, Secure, Path=/ — all correct.

OK · Refresh rotation implementation is correct: replaying an already-consumed refresh_token → 401 AND the previously-issued successor is also killed (family revoked on reuse). Verified in TestRefreshRotation::test_replay_rotated_refresh_returns_401.
OK · Login lockout after N failed attempts returns 429 rate_limited and is NOT bypassable by the X-RateLimit-Bypass header (test explicitly does not send bypass, still hits 429 within 6 attempts).
OK · Logout server-side revocation: old refresh cookie after logout returns 401 (session document removed / marked consumed).

OK · Password-change all-sessions revocation: after changing password in session-1, session-2's refresh_token is invalidated (returns 401). auth_sessions family revocation works across independently-issued sessions for the same user.

OK · Health endpoints hardened: /api/health returns {status:'ok', db:'connected', cid:...} with no exception-internals fields; /api/health/live returns 200; /api/health/ready returns 200 with checks payload including 'db' ok.
OK · WebSocket auth: cookie-auth to /api/ws works and emits {type:'connected'}; ?token= query connection is rejected with HTTP 403 (WS_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN env not set → query auth disabled).

OK · Frontend fails-fast at startup when REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL missing (throw new Error). Root ErrorBoundary catches render errors. UI verified during login → dashboard → Bot Config (Adaptive preset card renders as first item in 8-preset grid) → Scalp Fast Path → MT5 Accounts, all render cleanly (GET traffic uncorrupted by the origin bug because CSRF only checks mutating methods).
OK · Backend regression: 176/176 unit tests, 225/225 http-sample tests, 10/10 new iter-57 phase-1 tests. No regressions in the existing test surface (which does not send Origin headers).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce origin bug: (1) curl -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@trading.bot","password":"admin123"}'; (2) grab csrf_token from /tmp/c.txt; (3) curl -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/refresh -H 'X-CSRF-Token: <csrf>' -H 'Origin: https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com' → EXPECTED 200, ACTUAL 403 origin_not_allowed. Same request WITHOUT the -H 'Origin: ...' returns 200. Backend receives origin='https://algo-trade-135.cluster-12.preview.emergentcf.cloud' via the ingress rewrite; the CORS_ORIGINS allowlist only permits the .emergentagent.com domain. After main agent fixes: rerun tests/test_iter57_phase1_hardening.py plus an added case that sets Origin='https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com' explicitly on the refresh POST. UI regression check: click Apply on Adaptive preset in Bot Config → must NOT show the red 'Request blocked by CSRF protection' banner and active_preset must transition scalper→adaptive server-side (remember to restore to 'scalper' after). Live EAs on OnEquity Live have 1 open XAUUSD position — do NOT change bot config for that account. 2 live EAs are heartbeating; DO NOT touch bridge/execute endpoints.
rca of the issue: The Kubernetes ingress at algo-trade-135.preview.emergentagent.com terminates TLS and forwards to the backend pod, but along the way the Origin header the browser sent (https://stoic-trading-bot.preview.emergentagent.com) is REWRITTEN to the internal cluster canonical hostname (https://algo-trade-135.cluster-12.preview.emergentcf.cloud). The FastAPI csrf_middleware in /app/backend/server.py:77 calls security.csrf_check(request) which at security.py:139-143 does: `if allowed and origin and origin not in allowed: return 'origin_not_allowed'`. Because the rewritten Origin doesn't appear in the CORS_ORIGINS-derived allowed set, every cookie-authenticated mutating request is rejected regardless of a perfectly valid double-submit CSRF token pair. Mitigations (in priority order): (1) Best/short-term — add the cluster hostname (or a *.emergentcf.cloud wildcard suffix check) to _allowed_origins so both the public and cluster origins pass; (2) medium-term — since double-submit CSRF alone is defense-sufficient given SameSite=Lax/None+Secure cookies and CSRF cookie is JS-readable only via same-origin script (attackers can't read it), consider making origin_not_allowed non-fatal (log-only) and rely on the token-match check; (3) long-term — configure the ingress to preserve the client Origin header verbatim (via nginx `proxy_set_header Origin $http_origin;` or equivalent) so the same-string match works out of the box. This bug DOES NOT trigger in curl / requests / pytest because none of those clients send Origin by default — every existing pytest test passes because the `if allowed and origin` guard is false when Origin is absent, so the check falls through to the cookie/header token match which succeeds. Only a real browser (or curl -H 'Origin: ...') reveals the bug. The test suite has a coverage gap for browser-Origin scenarios.
